what: A Dante card's ARC 2.8.9 exchange with Dante Controller (start code 0x2809): every read Dante Controller sends a 2.8.9 device when it starts, with the card's reply. Dante Controller enables the device rename for this card.
captured: 2026-11-12, dstack #216, pktmon on the Dante Controller PC (Finding 16): Dante Controller's requests and the card's replies, paired by port and sequence. Read only: nothing was written to the card. Names are replaced with neutral ones of the same length and addresses with 192.0.2.x, so every offset holds; stale bytes the card leaves after a string's NUL (fragments of other names) are zeroed; other stale bytes the card leaves (an unused table slot, 0x2010's padding, 0x1003's bytes 20-27) are kept as captured, with the names in them replaced too. The reply's start code is the card's own: 0x2801 for 0x2204.
card_state: 2 TX and 2 RX channels, 96 kHz, 24 bit; TX channel 2 renamed (its default name differs); both RX channels subscribed (status 9) to one TX device; one RX flow (2 channels, 5 ms); two TX flows to two receivers.

second_device.what: The same 0x1000 and 0x2204 reads, read only from dev1 on 12.11.2026, from a 2.8.9 output adapter with 0 TX and 2 RX channels (no name in either reply).

layout.page request (0x2400, 0x3400, 0x3600): a 24-byte body: 6 zero bytes, 1, the media selector (1, audio), the first item (channel or flow, from 1), the last (0: to the end), then zeros. 0x2010 and 0x2204 take the 2.7 page body (0001, first, ..).
layout.page reply (0x2400, 0x3400, 0x3600): 6 zero bytes, [slots, count], `slots` packet offsets (only `count` used), then the strings, descriptors and records they point at.
layout.record: a chain of segments, each [its words, the words from it to the record's end] (the last segment's second byte may be 0).
layout.0x2400 record: 0x1414 (40 bytes): channel, 0, media 3, channel, 0, flags u32 (7), 0 u32, name offset (current name), format offset, 6 zero bytes, default-name offset, 8 zero bytes. Format: 16 bytes, as 2.7's common descriptor.
layout.0x3400 record: 0x141c (56 bytes): the 0x2400 record's first 40 bytes with flags 6, then [06 08], 0, TX channel offset, TX device offset, status (u16), receiver detail (u16, 0x0101), then [02 02], 0.
layout.0x3600 record: 0x1422 (68 bytes): flow, 0, media 3, flow, 0, flags u32 (1), 0 u32, name offset, format offset (8 bytes: rate u32, bits u32), latency ns u32, 12 zero bytes; [0a 0e], 10 zero bytes, slots, mapping offset, 4 zero bytes; [04 00], 0x0101, endpoint offset, 0. Then the endpoint (08 02 port ip, the receiver's own) and the mapping (first RX channel, bytes, next 0, then one byte per RX channel from the first: the flow slot feeding it, 0 for none).
layout.0x1000: the 2.7 counts (11 words, the first with 0x1000 set), zeros to body offset 34, the media record's offset (u16), 0, then a 0x1414 record: media 3, then pairs (1,1), (TX, RX channels), (2,2), (TX, RX flows), (2,2), (TX, RX: 0 on the TX side of a device without TX), (8,8), 8 zero bytes.
layout.0x1003: offsets 0x1c, 0x1c, 0x28, board name, revision, 8 bytes the card leaves stale (another read held the previous reply's bytes there), [05 00], name, factory name, name, 0, 0, then [0a 0a] 0 0x0403 0 0x2809 0x0204 0x1200 0x1004 0 0, then the name and the factory name in 32-byte fields, the board name and the revision.
layout.0x2010: the 2.7 page: [slots, count], (channel, channel, name offset) each, a zero word, the names; only the TX channels whose name is not the default are listed.
layout.0x2204: TX flow labels (netaudio's name): status OK, [slots, 0], `slots` zero words; the reply's start code is 0x2801 on both devices.
